items.b: GOLD LOST $150.10 AND SILVER 5.85%, THE WORST SESSION THIS TAPE HAS RECORDED
items.t: Against Thursday's marks of record, gold fell 3.2604% to $4,454.40 and silver 5.8507% to $66.253. In twenty-three sessions since 5 August the next-worst gold day is 0.9259% and the next-worst silver day 2.89%, so Friday is 3.52 and 2.02 times worse than anything before it. Platinum fell 3.3989% to $1,819.00. Palladium rose 1.7378% to $1,405.00, the only riser.

items.b: WARSH PUT A SEPTEMBER RATE RISE BACK ON THE BOARD, AND THE METAL REPRICED
items.t: The Federal Reserve chair told Jackson Hole that better summer PCE and CPI readings did not show underlying inflation improving, and that more than half of PCE items have risen above 3% over the past year against 32% in the two decades before the pandemic. CME FedWatch odds on a September hike moved from about 35.5% to 57.5%.

items.b: OFAC MOVED THE GRANDFATHERED RUSSIAN DIAMOND DEADLINE TO 1 SEPTEMBER 2027
items.t: General License No. 104B, issued 27 August, adds 365 days to a window that had closed on 1 September 2026. Stones of a carat and above must have left Russia before 1 March 2024 and half-to-one-carat goods before 1 September 2024, so the qualifying parcels will have sat 1,279 and 1,095 days by the new date. No carat weight for the remaining population has been published.

items.b: GIA AND GÜBELIN CONFIRMED ETHIOPIA AS A FOURTH SOURCE OF PARAÍBA TOURMALINE
items.t: The two laboratories announced jointly on 27 August, on separate samples, that Ethiopian copper-bearing tourmaline meets the accepted definition. Gübelin first saw the material in early May and GIA in June, later studying a parcel of more than 100 rough and faceted stones. Vanadium, lead and gallium separate it; no thresholds are published yet. SSEF called the same material inconclusive in June.

items.b: CHOW SANG SANG'S PROFIT ROSE 139% ON REVENUE UP 17%, AND THE MARGIN DOUBLED
items.t: The half to 30 June took HK$12.88 billion with HK$2.15 billion of profit, a net margin near 16.69% against about 8.17% a year earlier on this desk's arithmetic from the company's own figures. Mainland same-store sales went from 7% to 17% across the two quarters while Hong Kong and Macau fell from 46% to 30%. A net 47 shops closed.

items.b: A SOURCE THIS PAPER CITED WENT DARK AND CAME BACK, AND THE FIGURES CHECK OUT
items.t: diamondcitynews.com, cited on five Carat Capital articles, 301-redirected to an unrelated domain when Standards audited it on 28 August. This desk refetched it today: the site answers 200 and the cited Raksha Bandhan article renders. All four Ahmedabad counter figures Standards could not confirm - ₹1.7 lakh and ₹1.02 lakh gold, ₹2.45 lakh and ₹1.17 lakh silver - are present in the source's own Gujarati body text. No correction is required.
